note: Links only. Descriptions are written by KnightMatch; each site is the source of truth. Lab links carry still_says, a short phrase from the lab's page that the weekly check must still find. Re-check with: python -m knightmatch_scraper.check_links

sections.label: Start here
sections.title: Start with the Office of Undergraduate Research
sections.intro: OUR is UCF's home base for undergraduate research. If you're new to research, start here before emailing anyone.

links.title: Office of Undergraduate Research
links.description: Advising, workshops, funding, conferences and everything else OUR runs.

links.title: How to get started
links.description: OUR's guide to finding a first position, including how to write to a possible faculty mentor.

links.title: Workshops and deadlines
links.description: Dates for workshops like How to: Get Started in Undergraduate Research, plus grant and conference deadlines.

links.title: Meet a peer mentor
links.description: Students who already do research. Drop in or book through myKnightSTAR; the page has the hours and steps.

callout.title: The OUR research positions database
callout.body: OUR keeps its own list of faculty research positions. It is for UCF students only, and faculty contact details are protected on purpose. You get access by attending a How to: Get Started in Undergraduate Research workshop or meeting with an OUR peer mentor. KnightMatch never copies this database.

sections.label: Labs
sections.title: Labs that say they take undergraduates
sections.intro: Most labs never post openings. These pages say, in the lab's own words, that undergraduates can join and how to apply. We read each one by hand, and a weekly check flags any page that stops saying so. The lab's page always has the final word.

links.title: Psychology RA Match
links.description: One form for the department's labs: pick the labs you'd like, and faculty pull applications when a spot opens. Most spots are volunteer, the wait can be long, and every research assistant needs CITI training.
links.still_says: placed on a waiting list for future openings

links.title: Attention and Memory Lab
links.description: Says it is hiring undergraduate research assistants now, on a rolling basis, through an online application. Asks for a 3.0 GPA, 10 hours a week and at least a year.

links.title: Adult Development & Decision Lab
links.description: Aging and decision-making. Has research openings for undergraduates: send the lab manager a letter of interest to get the application link.

links.title: Virtual Avatar & Agent Interaction Lab
links.description: Virtual and augmented reality. Regularly takes undergraduate research assistants: fill out the lab's form, then email the director. Asks for a year.
links.still_says: opportunities to join VAAIL as a research assistant

links.title: Technology, Humans and Environments Lab
links.description: Eye tracking, virtual reality and how people search and interpret complex information. Has an undergraduate research assistant application on its home page.
links.still_says: Apply for an Undergraduate Research Assistant Position

links.title: Law, Applied Memory, and Psychology Lab
links.description: Psychology and the law, such as eyewitness memory. Undergraduate research assistants apply through an online form.
links.still_says: Research Assistants play an active role

links.title: DREAM Lab
links.description: Addiction research. Occasionally takes volunteer research assistants; start with the lab's survey.
links.still_says: occasionally accepts students for volunteer research assistant

links.title: ISUE Lab
links.description: 3D user interfaces, human-AI interaction and tutoring systems. Says it is always looking for undergraduates; contact the lab director.

links.title: Aquatic Biogeochemistry Lab
links.description: Chemical cycling where soil meets water. Takes undergraduates as volunteers, paid staff, independent study and honors students; start with the lab's online survey.

sections.label: Credit and pay

sections.intro: Research can count toward your degree, be a paid job, or come with money for supplies and travel.

links.title: Course credit for research (4912)

links.title: Federal Work Study for research assistants
links.description: If work study is in your aid package, it can pay your wages as a research assistant.

links.title: Student research grants
links.description: Money for materials, equipment or research travel, applied for through InfoReady.

links.title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship
links.description: Spend a summer on your own project with a faculty mentor, ending in a poster presentation.
